title: Book 3 — Thalia, Chapter 405
paragraphs: The Persians provided this water supply route through the desert after they conquered Egypt. But at the time of Cambyses' invasion, when the route had no water stations, Cambyses took Phanes' advice and sent a messenger to the Arabian king to request safe passage, giving and receiving pledges of friendship. No people revere the oath of friendship more than the Arabs. When two men wish to make a pledge, a third man stands between them. Using a sharp stone, he makes a cut on the inside of each man's palm near the base of the middle fingers. He takes a thread from each man's cloak, dips it in blood, and smears seven stones placed between them, invoking Dionysus and Ourania. When this ceremony is complete, the man who made the pledge introduces the foreigner (or fellow citizen, if the pledge is between citizens) to his friends, and they too consider themselves bound by the oath. The Arabs recognize only two gods: Dionysus and Ourania. They say they cut their hair in the same style as Dionysus, shaving it in a circle around the head and cutting the temples short. They call Dionysus Orotalt and Ourania Alilat.
